instrument_name: NH RSA 275:43 Weekly or Biweekly (payment of wages; methods incl. direct deposit and payroll card; vacation/sick/holiday pay as wages)
figure_or_rule_carried: Wages due within 8 days after the workweek (weekly) or within 15 days (biweekly), on predesignated regular paydays; less frequent (at least monthly) only by written permission of the Labor Commissioner (IV). Methods: cash, EFT, direct deposit with written employee authorization to bank of employee choice, payroll card (one free full withdrawal per pay period, written voluntary consent, not a condition of hire, fee list disclosure, opt-out any time) or check; if EFT/direct deposit/card is used the employer must offer the check option. V: vacation, severance, personal days, holiday, sick pay and expenses are wages when due under employment practice or policy.

instrument_name: NH RSA 275:44 Employees Separated From Payroll Before Pay Days
figure_or_rule_carried: Discharge: wages in full within 72 hours. Resignation: by the next regular payday; if the employee gave at least one pay period's notice, within 72 hours. Layoff or labor-dispute suspension: next regular payday. Willful failure: liquidated damages 10% of unpaid wages per day (except Sundays/holidays) capped at the unpaid amount.

instrument_name: NH RSA chapter 279 Minimum Wage Law: 279:21 (minimum hourly rate, tipped, exemptions, overtime), 279:21-a (meal/lodging credits), 279:26-b (tips), 279:27 (records)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage = federal minimum wage as amended (USD 7.25 under FLSA; NH has no own figure). Tipped (restaurant, hotel, motel, inn, cabin, ballroom; >USD 30/month tips): base not less than 45% of the applicable minimum (= USD 3.27) until the federal minimum rises above the 2021-07-23 level, then the federal minimum direct wage but never below USD 3.27. Exempt from NH minimum: household/domestic, farm labor, outside salesmen, summer-camp staff for minors, newsboys, non-professional ski patrol, golf caddies; learners <6 months (75% on application) and persons 16 or under (75%). Overtime 1.5x over 40 h/week, but 279:21 VIII(b) excludes employees of FLSA-covered employers (FLSA governs; fluctuating-workweek method barred for delivery drivers/sales merchandisers). Meal/lodging credits (hotel/restaurant): full board+room 45.00/week, meals 1.88/meal, lodging 1.80/day. Records of hours and wages kept 3 years; electronic retention allowed.

instrument_name: NH Lab 800 rules (Lab 803.01 payment of wages, 803.03 notification and records, 803.05 exemptions)
authority: NH Department of Labor / Office of Legislative Services
figure_or_rule_carried: Biweekly pay: first payment within 8 days (incl. Sunday) after the work weeks; petition for semi-monthly/monthly pay lists 7 data items and is granted case by case. Discharge: 72 hours, in person or by mail at employee's choice. At hire and before any change: written notice of rate, pay basis, day and place of payment and method of computing wages; written or posted description of vacation, holiday, sick, bonus, severance, personal-day, expense and pension policies; signed copy of the notices kept on file. Written statement of deductions (RSA 275:48/49 IV). Hours records for non-FLSA-exempt employees kept at least 3 years; altered time records initialled by employee.

Wage-payment chapter excludes employers of domestic labor in the employer's home and farm employers with fewer than 5 employees; employee definition with a 7-criterion independent-contractor test (a)-(g); wages include health/welfare and pension fund contributions under agreement.

instrument_name: NH RSA 282-A:117-a Employment Reports to NHES; State Directory of New Hires
figure_or_rule_carried: New-hire report to NHES within 20 days of hire or rehire (electronic filers: 2 monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart); also independent contractors (non-casual) when payment is expected to exceed USD 2,500. Content: full name, address, SSN, first day of work; employer name, address, federal and state ID. W-4 copy acceptable. Multistate employers may designate one state (notify HHS).

instrument_name: NH RSA chapter 282-A Unemployment Compensation: 282-A:9 (employment, localization, exclusions), 282-A:15 (wages), 282-A:69 (payment of contributions)
figure_or_rule_carried: 282-A:69 I: contributions 2.7% (subject to experience rating RSA 282-A:79-90) on wages up to USD 14,000 per individual per calendar year; contributions shall NOT be deducted in whole or part from employee wages (no employee share); for the 14,000 base, wages include service subject to another state's employment security law (credit for wages reported to another state). Base is a fixed statutory figure, not indexed. 282-A:9 I: localization test (localized / base of operations / direction and control). Exclusions incl. domestic service unless cash >= USD 1,000 in a quarter; services of minister/religious order; students employed by their school; individual employed by son/daughter/spouse and child under 21 employed by parent; agricultural labor covered per FUTA 3306(c)(1). 282-A:15: wages include bonuses, board, lodging, payment in kind; exclude employer payments under a plan for retirement, third-party sickness/disability, medical/hospitalization, SUB, death benefits, employer-paid FICA. No express exclusion for employee elective deferrals (401(k)/125) located in 282-A:15.

instrument_name: NH RSA chapter 458-B Income Assignment (child/spousal support)
figure_or_rule_carried: Arrearage add-on at least 20% of current support; lump-sum payments (severance, accumulated sick/vacation pay, bonuses, commissions) subject to assignment up to arrearage when obligor non-compliant; total withheld capped at 15 U.S.C. 1673(b). Priority: current support, health insurance/cash medical, arrears, other. Employer: implement no later than the first pay period occurring 14 days after notice mailed; remit at the same time the obligor is paid; support withholding has priority over other state legal process; employer may deduct a fee of USD 1.00 per withholding; notify within 15 days of termination with last known address and new employer; administrative fine USD 100 per pay period per employee for willful failure; discharge/discipline for withholding = misdemeanor, fine up to USD 1,000.

instrument_name: NH RSA 512:21 List of Exemptions (trustee process / wage garnishment for creditor debts)
figure_or_rule_carried: Wages for labor performed after service of the writ are exempt (I). Wages earned before service are exempt except in actions on a debt on a New Hampshire court judgment; then 50 x the FLSA minimum hourly wage per week is exempt (50 x 7.25 = USD 362.50/week) and paid on the usual payday (II). Loan contracts under RSA 399-A: USD 50/week exempt (IX). More protective than CCPA 30x. Payroll accounts exempt (XI).

instrument_name: NH RSA chapter 359-C Right to Privacy: 359-C:19-21 security breach notification
figure_or_rule_carried: Personal information = name + SSN, driver's licence/government ID, or financial account number with access code (unencrypted). Breach of computerized data: notify affected individuals as soon as possible when misuse occurred or is reasonably likely; notify the NH Attorney General (or primary regulator) with anticipated notice date and approximate number of NH individuals; data maintainers (e.g. payroll processors) notify the owner immediately. No pay-statement SSN-truncation rule found in this chapter.

instrument_name: NH RSA chapter 275 Protective Legislation (consolidated chapter, Wayback 2026-03-19): 275:30-a, 275:37-d, 275:43-a, 275:43-c, 275:47, 275:57, 275:78-83
figure_or_rule_carried: 30-minute meal period after 5 consecutive hours (unless eating while working is permitted). Reporting pay: minimum 2 hours at regular rate when employee reports at employer's request (not counties/municipalities). 275:37-d: employers with 50+ employees sponsoring Granite State FML insurance must restore the employee and continue health insurance (eff 2021-07-01, am. 2023). 275:43-c: small employers (2+ NH employees, no employer health plan) may set up a premium-only section 125 plan; employees working >15 h/week may buy small-group coverage by payroll deduction. Deceased employee wages up to USD 3,000 payable without probate (am. 2024-09-10). Expense reimbursement within 30 days of proof. Lactation (eff 2025-07-01, employers with 6+ NH employees): unpaid break of about 30 minutes per 3 hours worked, for 1 year after birth; written policy made available at hire. Pay-disclosure protection (275:41-b). The chapter snapshot of 2026-03-19 shows no RSA 275:37-f (parental medical leave), so that 2026 provision was not read here.

instrument_name: NH parental medical leave (unpaid, up to 25 hours; employers with 20+ employees), reported as RSA 275:37-f enacted by 2025 HB 2, eff 2026-01-01
authority: NH General Court (statute not read); leads: law-firm alerts (Nixon Peabody 2025-09-04, Duane Morris, Hinckley Allen)
figure_or_rule_carried: LEAD ONLY: employers with 20+ employees must allow up to 25 hours of UNPAID leave in the year after birth for childbirth/postpartum/infant medical appointments. No payroll calculation impact beyond unpaid-absence handling. Statute page: direct 403; Wayback copy 2026-06-17 returned the 403 page.

instrument_name: NHES Employer Handbook NHES 0041 R-8/16 (listed by NHES as current Employer Handbook on 2026-10-30): taxes, new hire, mass layoff, posting chapters
article_or_section: Handbook pp. 6-10, 14; attachments IV, V, VII, VIII
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer Quarterly Tax and Wage Report (Part 1 tax, Part 2 wages; every quarter even with no employment; gross wages of every employee reported, tax only on excess-adjusted taxable wages) and full payment due on the last day of the month following the quarter (Q1 due April 30); WebTax filers have 2 extra days; 30-day filing extension on application + USD 50 fee before due date (filing only). Late filing fee 10% of tax due, minimum USD 25 per occurrence; interest 1% per month on unpaid tax; accounts out of balance at April 30 get the highest schedule rate for the July-June rate year. Tax = net taxable wages x UI rate, then AC split. New hire: online, mail/fax W-4 (W-9 for contractors), or electronic in 2 monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart. Preliminary Mass Layoff Notice when 25+ laid off in a week for 7+ days (vacation shutdown, closure, furlough). Unemployment Notice poster mandatory at each establishment. Employer must give partially employed claimants proof of earnings. Highest earned rate 7.0%. Procedural/2016 edition: fee and interest figures to be re-verified against RSA 282-A:? or Emp 300 rules.

Under 16: certificate required (except work for parents/grandparents/guardian, casual work, farm labor); hours 7 a.m.-9 p.m., max 3 h on school days and 23 h in school weeks, 8 h on non-school days, 48 h/week in vacations. Under 12: only family, casual or newspaper delivery. 16-17 enrolled in school: max 35 h in a 5-day school week; max 6 consecutive days / 48 h per week in vacations (summer = June 1 to Labor Day; camp exception). 16-17 without diploma/GED: signed parental permission kept on file. No youth in hazardous occupations except approved programmes. (Pay impact: minimum wage for 16 and under is 75% of the statutory minimum per RSA 279:21 V, register US-NHS5-003.)

instrument_name: NH RSA 21-I:103 Granite State Paid Family Leave Plan: coverage for other employers and individual employees
figure_or_rule_carried: Voluntary FMLI (no mandatory payroll levy): private employers with more than 50 employees may sponsor coverage by contracting directly with the state's carrier; contributory, partially contributory or non-contributory plans and payroll deduction/premium remittance procedures set by the commissioner. Employees of non-sponsoring employers may buy individual coverage through the NHES-administered purchasing pool (RSA 282-B): 7-month waiting period, 1-week elimination period, 60-day open enrollment; premium capped at USD 5 per subscriber per week. Payroll impact only where the employer sponsors a contributory plan (voluntary post-tax/agreed deduction under RSA 275:48).

instrument_name: NH DRA: Granite State Paid Family and Medical Leave Plan Tax Credit (RSA 77-E:3-e)
figure_or_rule_carried: Business Enterprise Tax credit = 50% of the premium paid by a sponsoring employer for FMLI coverage under RSA 21-I:103, for the taxable period in which paid. Entity-level BET item, not a payroll calculation (BET excluded from payroll scope per US-OWN-007).
